references.text: Describes God's gift of 'heavenly bread' (manna) that satisfied the people, a direct precursor to Jesus' claim to be the true bread that gives life.
Teaches that man does not live by bread alone, but by God's word, which Jesus fulfills by identifying himself as the bread of life.
Invites those who are thirsty to come and drink without money, an image Jesus makes concrete by promising that whoever believes in him will never thirst again.
Prophesies that God's people will not suffer from hunger or thirst, a prophecy fulfilled by Jesus being the source of eternal satisfaction.
Jesus promises that whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst, a direct parallel to the promise that whoever believes in him will never thirst again.
Revisits the motif of 'water from the spring of life' given freely, as a fulfillment of Jesus' promise that whoever believes in him will never thirst again.
